A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OccMamba research and are readable throughout, including equations, figures and tables. The core methods and three benchmarks align. V2 includes supplementary Sections 6.1–6.5; the supplied v1 refers to supplementary results but has no attached appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original OccMamba benchmark results, reordering and MonoScene ablations, and GPU memory and inference-time measurements in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results and additional component, reordering, loss and label-quality experiments, including supplementary RayIoU results.

M1.justification: V2 inserts a local context processor between the hierarchical Mamba module and occupancy head. It processes sliding XY patches with Mamba blocks, reassembles and concatenates their features, and applies a 1×1×1 convolution (Sections 3.2–3.3). This adds a substantive processing stage; the height-prioritized reordering and training losses remain.

E1.justification: The same three datasets remain. However, v1 evaluates OccMamba with camera-only, LiDAR-only and fused inputs on OpenOccupancy, whereas v2 retains only fused-input OccMamba evaluations there. Both OpenOccupancy annotation versions remain represented, and SemanticPOSS retains its LiDAR-only evaluation.

E2.justification: SparseOcc is added to the main OpenOccupancy comparison in Table 1. The M-CONet comparison under v0.1 annotations in v1 Table 2 is absent from v2's corresponding supplementary evaluation. Additional Z-order alternatives appear in v2 Table 8. SemanticKITTI and SemanticPOSS retain their baseline sets.

E3.justification: The reported default annotations for OpenOccupancy ablations and efficiency comparisons change from v0.1 to v0.0. New supplementary experiments introduce RayIoU@0.2m and loss ablations using 20% of the training set. Core benchmark splits, SemanticKITTI test-time augmentation and measurement hardware remain unchanged; newly disclosed optimization settings are documentation additions.

E4.justification: V2 adds component controls separating the hierarchical module and local context processor, extends the MonoScene ablation, and tests Z-order alternatives and individual training losses. Section 6.3 additionally examines label quality and geometric accuracy, with a distant-object reconstruction example. These substantially expand the evidence explaining individual design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. V2's descriptions of significant improvements do not introduce statistical testing.

E6.justification: The main OpenOccupancy fusion result changes from 33.7 IoU/25.1 mIoU to 35.7/26.2 for the revised 384-dimensional model. Its reported inference time also changes from 398.1 to 448.3 ms. V2 adds numerous ablation and class-wise results, while SemanticKITTI and SemanticPOSS headline scores remain 24.6 and 23.4. Table 1 also changes Co-Occ's sidewalk score from 25.5 to 5.5 without changing its reported mean.

T1.justification: V2 adds formal definitions of local window extraction and patch processing/reassembly in Equations 12–14. This is a limited mathematical extension accompanying the new component. The existing SSM, Mamba-block and loss mathematics remain equivalent, and neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The first-Mamba, height-prioritized reordering and three-benchmark state-of-the-art claims remain. V2 adds local context processing to its explicit design contributions and removes the earlier claim of OpenOccupancy superiority across all three input-modality settings, focusing its own reported comparisons on fusion.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting Hilbert ordering to locality and relating the local processor's benefits to geometric coherence, occlusion-sensitive evaluation and annotation noise. Its efficiency discussion also replaces v1's approximately 20% training-memory saving for the 384-dimensional model with an acknowledgment of memory usage similar to M-CONet.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 newly documents AdamW, learning rate, weight decay, backbone pretraining and learning-rate scaling, cosine scheduling, warmup and 20 training epochs. V2 also specifies local processor window sizes and replaces the future code-release promise with a stated release and repository address. These substantially improve documented reproducibility without establishing that previously unspecified settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references concerning 3D pretraining, multimodal fusion and SparseOcc, and supplies citations for several baselines already evaluated in v1. The related-work categories and positioning as a Mamba-based occupancy predictor remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. V2 refines architecture terminology around the OccMamba encoder, expands SSM explanations, revises the abstract and experimental discussion, and adds organized supplementary subsections. Author, affiliation and citation-style edits are also present; the retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 1(c) changes from a modality-based comparison to an IoU–mIoU scatter plot, and Figure 2 is substantially redrawn to display the local processor. V2 adds Figure 5 and several ablation and class-wise tables, restructures the MonoScene table with component columns, and changes document formatting. Figures 3 and 4 largely retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility and makes design choices easier to assess through component, loss and label-quality analyses. These gains are tempered by removed unimodal OpenOccupancy evaluations and new reporting inconsistencies. Table 7 implies about 65% of M-CONet's inference time, while the prose claims 35%; Table 1 changes Co-Occ's sidewalk score without updating its mean. The stronger documentation and diagnostic evidence support a limited net improvement.
